status: formula-corrected immutable V2 ledger; V3 adaptive Batch2 model is a separate addendum

scope.machine_counters: unavailable: old-platform CSV and perf-paranoid-4 counters are absent; physical DRAM/cache-miss values below are bounds or estimates only
scope.source_anchor_note: All V2 line references are against immutable snapshots at bench/8454h/versions/v2/, not the evolving production working tree.

notation.M: rows(A), N: columns(B), K: reduction; default square case M=N=K=n
notation.d: FP64 budget depth: p6=3, p10=4, p15=5, p21=6
notation.p: number of independent BF16 product pairs: FP32=6, FP64=d(d+1)/2
notation.Q: logical bytes transferred by instruction-level tile loads/stores or SIMD reconstruction, not DRAM bytes
notation.Weff: 2MNK effective mathematical FLOPs (FP32/FP64 output GEMM accounting convention)
notation.Wamx: 2MNK*p BF16 product-pair FLOPs executed across AMX TDP instructions; report separately from Weff. Weff undercounts AMX component-product work by factor p.
notation.all_bytes: decimal bytes; formulas count logical payload and exclude line fills, write allocation, coherence and allocator effects
notation.Mp: ceil(M/32)*32, output rows actually visited by 32x32 AMX/SIMD microtiles
notation.Np: ceil(N/32)*32, output columns actually visited by 32x32 AMX/SIMD microtiles
notation.Kp32: ceil(K/32)*32, reduction work issued by AMX K32 steps
notation.r: ceil(K/256), number of outer BK256 accumulation chunks; retained as the existing r symbol

fp32_six_kernel.facts: 24 TDPBF16PS instructions and 14 tile loads per K32 (six A tiles, six B tiles, with two operand tiles reused twice); four tile stores per call

fp64_product_kernel.facts: 4 TDPBF16PS instructions and 4 tile loads per K32; four tile stores per call

fp32_projection.facts: three BF16 slices are produced for each FP32 element; direct path writes panel layout without a later dense-to-panel pack

fp64_projection.facts: six projection rounds are always evaluated and residuals advance through all six; only d slices are stored; aligned direct path fuses projection and panel placement

packing.facts: separate path reads dense split slices and writes padded 256x256 panels; K/N/M tails are zero padded

output_path.facts: per 32x32 micro result is accumulated in a 32/128 cache block; whole cache block is zeroed and valid rows copied to dense result, then result copied to caller C

actual_amx_bf16_pair_flops.formula_useful: Wamx_useful=2*M*N*K*p (useful scalar product FLOPs; p component-product pairs)
actual_amx_bf16_pair_flops.note: Wamx_useful is distinct from effective GEMM work Weff=2MNK. The issued count includes M/N edge microtile padding and final K32 padding; it equals exact TDP instruction count times 16,384 FLOPs per instruction.

tdp_instruction_count.note: Counts the four 16x16 quadrants across each 32x32 output microtile, per K32 step. This is an exact instruction count for issued work. Useful Wamx uses MNK; Wamx_executed uses Mp*Np*Kp32.

simd_reconstruction_work.formula: FP32: Mp*Np*r scalar float adds; FP64: p*Mp*Np*r scalar double adds plus p*Mp*Np*r float-to-double value conversions
simd_reconstruction_work.note: The kernel updates full 32x32 microtiles, including output edge padding. FP32 has one SIMD accumulation per BK256 chunk. FP64 has one ordered add and one converted float value per independent product and output lane.

cold_materialized_traffic_scenario.formula: source + explicit preparation streams + packed-panel materialization + result/C streams; scenario estimate, not a measured DRAM count or strict lower bound

fp32.packed_panel_write: 6*Ppanel bytes: three stored slices, each 2 bytes, over Ppanel aggregate A+B BF16 elements per slice
fp32.result_and_C_logical_streams: 16*M*N result-buffer and caller-C copy streams; block accumulator streams accounted separately

fp64_depth_d.result_and_C_logical_streams: 32*M*N because block-to-result and result-to-C each read+write double values
fp64_depth_d.note: In a warm-cache repeated call (for example N=1024 with panels retained in cache), physical DRAM traffic can be far below these materialized logical streams. Packed writes/reads are not per-call compulsory DRAM bytes.

cold_materialized_traffic_scenario.Ppanel: ceil(M/256)*ceil(K/256)*65536 + ceil(K/256)*ceil(N/256)*65536 BF16 elements across A and B per slice
cold_materialized_traffic_scenario.warning: This describes logical/materialized streams under a cold or capacity-miss scenario. It is neither a strict lower bound nor a measurement. Physical traffic depends on residency, write allocation, reuse and eviction; Qtile/QSIMD are instruction-level demands, not DRAM bounds.
cold_materialized_traffic_scenario.note: S=M*K+K*N counts scalar source elements before dtype sizing; source-read bytes are separate. Ppanel counts padded BF16 elements across A+B for one slice, each 2 bytes. FP32 stores 3 slices, so its panel write is 6*Ppanel bytes. This cold/materialized scenario is not a per-call compulsory DRAM lower bound.

fp32_general_split_then_pack.packed_panel_write: 6*Ppanel bytes: three stored slices, each 2 bytes, over Ppanel aggregate A+B BF16 elements per slice
fp32_general_split_then_pack.note: Dense slice reads/writes are useful payload; panel writes include padded slots. S counts scalar inputs; each stored BF16 slice element occupies 2 bytes.

fp32_aligned_direct.packed_panel_write: 6*S bytes: three stored slices, each 2 bytes, over S aggregate A+B source elements
fp32_aligned_direct.note: Eligible when min(M,N)>=1024 and M,N,K divisible by 256; projection and panel placement fused.

fp64_general_split_then_pack_depth_d.residual_array: initialization: 8S write; six rounds each read 8S for max collection, read another 8S for projection, then write 8S updated residual: 152S logical residual-array bytes, with S=M*K+K*N
fp64_general_split_then_pack_depth_d.note: Six rounds execute even for d=3/4/5. The two residual reads in each round are distinct source loops in split_fp64. This is logical traffic; residual may remain cache-resident.

fp64_aligned_direct_depth_d.residual_array: initialization: 8S write; six rounds each read 8S for projection and write 8S updated residual, with next-max fused into that pass: 104S logical residual-array bytes
fp64_aligned_direct_depth_d.packed_panel_write: 2*d*S bytes (d slices per A/B source element, 2 bytes each)
fp64_aligned_direct_depth_d.note: Projection fused with panel placement; six-round residual evolution remains. Source read is counted separately.

projection_actual_logical.Ppanel: ceil(M/256)*ceil(K/256)*65536 + ceil(K/256)*ceil(N/256)*65536 BF16 elements across A and B per slice
projection_actual_logical.Ppanel_unit_note: Ppanel is the aggregate BF16 element count across padded A and B layouts for one slice; multiply by 2 for bytes.

amx_tile_store.note: Each call stores four 16x16 FP32 accumulator tiles. Counts include padded 32x32 output microtiles; FP64 stores p times per BK256 chunk.

reuse_bounds.per_k_call_logical_load: Exact instruction payload above; repeated panel addresses across neighboring output microtiles are not deduplicated.
reuse_bounds.L1: Adjacent microtiles may reuse A or B panels depending on schedule and cache capacity; this does not remove tileload instructions.
reuse_bounds.L2_L3_DRAM: The cache level serving each payload is unknown. Exact logical operand payload is not a DRAM bound.

fp32_each_microtile_product.formula_per_scalar_output_product: 12 bytes per padded output scalar per BK256 chunk
fp32_each_microtile_product.note: 32x32 FP32 micro is accumulated into FP32 cache block once per K256 chunk.

fp64_each_microtile_product.formula_per_scalar_output_product: 20 bytes per padded output scalar per product in V2 (4-byte micro read + 8-byte double read + 8-byte double write)
fp64_each_microtile_product.note: The 4-byte float micro value is converted to double, then added to the double block. V2 issues one accumulator block read and write per product; the V3 Wide Batch2 variant is described separately below.

cache_block_zero_and_result_copy.zero: sizeof(T)*cb^2 bytes written per output block, cb=32 for min(M,N)<1024 else 128
cache_block_zero_and_result_copy.block_to_result: sizeof(T)*M*N logical source read plus same-size result write; full blocks copy valid rows only
cache_block_zero_and_result_copy.result_to_C: sizeof(T)*M*N result read plus same-size C write
cache_block_zero_and_result_copy.combined_valid_payload: FP32: zero bytes sizeof(float)*cb^2*ceil(M/cb)*ceil(N/cb); copies=16*M*N. FP64: zero bytes sizeof(double)*cb^2*ceil(M/cb)*ceil(N/cb); copies=32*M*N. Private result and caller C are both double in FP64.

simd_reconstruction_and_output.write_allocate_RFO: Cold single-pass temporal-store scenario: about one cache-line read-for-ownership per cold line written. This is an estimate scenario, not a physical upper bound; repeated eviction, coherence transfers and false sharing can add ownership traffic. Excluded from logical-byte totals.
simd_reconstruction_and_output.padded_output_elements: Mp*Np where Mp=ceil(M/32)*32 and Np=ceil(N/32)*32; microtile accumulation covers edge padding too
simd_reconstruction_and_output.simd_operation_counts: FP32 adds=Mp*Np*r; FP64 conversions=p*Mp*Np*r and ordered double adds=p*Mp*Np*r. Counts are values over padded output lanes, not FLOP-equivalent work.

roofline_model.do_not_merge: AMX BF16 TDP work uses P_AMX and Q_tileload at L1/L2 boundaries; AVX-512 projection/reconstruction uses P_SIMD and its own traffic. AMX and SIMD overlap is unknown, so report separate stage bounds and sum serial phase bounds only as a conservative model; do not divide combined work by a single peak.
roofline_model.observable_timing: CSV split_s_mean, pack_s_mean, compute_recon_s_mean, profile_total_s_mean, api_call_wall_s_mean; compute_recon currently combines AMX+SIMD+result/C copies, so it cannot identify their overlap or individual time.
roofline_model.overhead_residual: api_call_wall_s_mean - profile_total_s_mean is a measured scope delta, not pure dispatch overhead; profile phases and API wall have distinct wrappers and noise.

calibration_data.availability: 20 complete rows: 4 sizes x 5 product budgets, 64 threads, 5 repetitions; use phase times to fit effective per-stage ceilings, but not to infer cache miss or DRAM bandwidth without counters.
calibration_data.mkl: mkl_gemm_s measures MKL GEMM only; our full profile includes projection, packing and output copies, so whole-API speed ratios are not like-for-like compute ceilings.

candidate_models.change_axis: add a direct residual-to-panel fused path for divisible matrix dimensions and a tile-buffered fused tail path
candidate_models.predicted_cost_removed: general FP32: 6S dense slice reread + 6S intermediate writes; general FP64: 2dS slice write + 2dS pack read
candidate_models.measure: split, pack, API wall on N=256/1024/4096/8192; padding bytes and actual memory traffic separately

candidate_models.change_axis: test cache-resident or blocked residual passes with next-max reduction fused into each projection pass
candidate_models.predicted_cost_removed: reduce residual-array reread/write round-trip or improve sequential locality; six semantic projections still required
candidate_models.risk: global max / sigma dependencies require round barriers; only streaming/layout changes are candidates
candidate_models.measure: split phase, LLC/DRAM counters when available

candidate_models.change_axis: accumulate multiple 32x32 micro outputs in a register/L1-friendly output tile and reduce repeated FP64 block read/write
candidate_models.predicted_cost_removed: FP64 logical reconstruction cost currently 20*p bytes per output per BK256; target fewer repeated double block loads/stores
candidate_models.measure: compute_recon phase plus SIMD instruction and L1 traffic counters

candidate_models.change_axis: compare loop_order=0 vs product/K-block-major scheduling and M/N tile ordering with panel working-set estimates
candidate_models.predicted_cost_removed: improve L1/L2 service of repeated A/B operands; tileload instruction count unchanged
candidate_models.measure: L1/L2 hit/miss counters; separate effective bandwidth estimates from exact tileload bytes

candidate_models.change_axis: choose cache block from private-block bytes, result-store traffic and thread working set; candidates 32/64/128/256 as models, with current 128 retained as baseline
candidate_models.predicted_cost_removed: reduce zero/copy overhead or improve cache residency; for FP64 private block grows as 8*cb^2 bytes per active worker
candidate_models.measure: phase time, LLC misses, RFO/ writeback counters; avoid cache macro-only retuning without this model

uncertainty.physical_dram: unknown; cold/materialized logical stream scenario is given, not a strict bound or measurement; cache eviction/reuse cannot be deduced from source or CSV
uncertainty.cache_misses: unknown; tileload address/byte payload is exact at instruction level; which cache level services it is hardware/schedule dependent
uncertainty.tileload_vs_cacheline: 1024 B is architectural tile payload; actual cache-line requests can differ due alignment, panel reuse and implementation
uncertainty.simd_overlap: unmeasured because compute_recon timing aggregates AMX, reconstruction and copies

formula_corrections.baseline: Immutable V2 formulas above replace earlier derived expressions; raw kernel instruction facts in evidence.fp32_six_kernel and evidence.fp64_product_kernel are unchanged.

corrections.correct_expression: p*Mp*Np*ceil(K/256) of each; conversion and add counts remain distinct from AMX work
6*Ppanel and direct 6*S; each of 3 stored slices is 2 bytes
Use Mp,Np for full 32x32 tile operations; retain useful MNK for Weff and Wamx_useful. Use Kp32 only for TDP work.

v3_adaptive_batch64_model.scope: Separate adaptive V3 addendum; does not alter immutable V2 kernel facts or formulas above.
v3_adaptive_batch64_model.wide_dispatch: Wide iff min(M,N)>=4096. FP32 and FP64 depth<=4 use output block cb=128 rows by cbn=512 columns; FP64 depth 5/6 use cb=128 by cbn=256. Per row the accumulator stride adds one 64-byte pad: 64/sizeof(T) elements. Below the Wide threshold, V2 cache-block selection remains.
v3_adaptive_batch64_model.unchanged_work: The AMX product pairs, TDP instruction counts, operand tileloads, AMX tile stores, product sequence, K/BK loops, FP32 SIMD additions, and FP64 conversion/add counts are unchanged. The padded output microtile geometry for work counts remains Mp*Np.

fp64_wide_batch2.dispatch: Only Wide FP64 uses Batch=2; non-Wide FP64 keeps Batch=1. Every product still stores its FP32 32x32 micro result and component additions remain in the original product order.
fp64_wide_batch2.products_per_accumulator_block_round: ceil(p/2); p=6,10,15,21 therefore use 3,5,8,11 rounds, with a one-product tail for odd p.
fp64_wide_batch2.micro_float_reads: 4*p*Mp*Np*r logical bytes; conversions remain p*Mp*Np*r values.
fp64_wide_batch2.double_accumulator_reads_and_writes: 16*ceil(p/2)*Mp*Np*r logical bytes (8-byte read + 8-byte write per output lane per batch).
fp64_wide_batch2.saved_vs_v2: 16*(p-ceil(p/2))*Mp*Np*r logical bytes; p adds and conversions are unchanged.
fp64_wide_batch2.scratch: Two aligned FP32 32x32 product results reserve 2*32*32*4=8192 bytes per active worker instead of 4096 bytes for one result. The stores/reads are already represented by AMX tile-store and SIMD micro-read terms; do not count a second scratch copy.

wide_private_block_storage.f32: Reserved 128*(512+16)*4=270336 bytes per worker; zeroed active block is the same size.
wide_private_block_storage.f64_depth_le4: Reserved 128*(512+8)*8=532480 bytes; active stride/zeroed block uses 128*(512+8)*8=532480 bytes.
wide_private_block_storage.f64_depth_5_or_6: Reserved maximum remains 532480 bytes; active stride/zeroed block uses 128*(256+8)*8=270336 bytes.
wide_private_block_storage.note: These are stack block capacities/logical zero stores, not measured cache residency or DRAM traffic.

v3_adaptive_batch64_model.calibration_gate: The exact full-buffer binary comparison and transactional checks are recorded in bench/8454h/roofline/binary_gate.json; no-OpenMP subset in noomp_gate.json; formal 47-case cache 2GiB/0 gate in extended47_cache_gate.json. Production library hash matches fresh production build.
